issues.detail: The Greek 'ουχι η καρδια ημων καιομενη ην εν ημιν' is a rhetorical question/exclamation meaning 'Was not our heart burning within us?' (expressing that it WAS burning). The Vietnamese translation 'há chẳng nóng nảy sao?' (Is our heart not burning?) renders it as a present-tense inquiry about current state, whereas the Greek uses the imperfect tense ('ην') to refer to the experience while they were walking.
The Vietnamese translation omits the specific past tense aspect of the Greek 'ην' (was), which indicates a continuous state in the past.
